summary: Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under M. H. Krishna at Maharaja's College, Mysore from circa 1934 to 1938.

Jayandra Soni worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning doctorates at Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University. He lectured at the University of Marburg (1991–2012) and held posts at the University of Innsbruck and the International Association of Sanskrit Studies.

Jaś Elsner is a scholar of archaeology, art history, and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, London, and Harvard, his career includes fellowships at Cambridge and posts at the Courtauld Institute, Corpus Christi College, and the University of Oxford as professor.
Jean Dantinne was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte and served as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Deloche was an Indologist and historian. He directed the Alliance Française of Madras (1962–1966) and served as a researcher and associate member at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, as well as an associate member at the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and historian who studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He directed EPHE's Indian philology chair, the French Institute of Pondicherry (1955–1977), the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1956–1977), and held a chair at Collège de France.

Jean Kellens is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology linguistics. He studied at the University of Liège and FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, later holding academic posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, Liège, and the Collège de France.

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under C. C. Uhlenbeck and Hendrik Kern at the University of Amsterdam. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and directed Leiden University and the Kern Institute.

Jean Przyluski was a linguist, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at EPHE under Henri Hubert and Marcel Mauss. He held chairs at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France.

Jean-Baptiste Biot was a scientist and Indologist who studied under Gaspard Monge and Pierre-Simon Laplace at École Polytechnique. He held professorships at the École Centrale de Beauvais, the Science Faculty of Paris, and the Collège de France (1800–1862).

Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the École du Louvre and the University of Paris. He served as director (1986–2004) and president (circa 1986–2008) of the Musée Guimet.

Jean-François Lyotard was a philosopher who studied at the University of Paris and Paris Nanterre University. He held academic posts at Paris Nanterre, Paris 8 University Vincennes-Saint-Denis (1972–1987), UC Irvine, and Emory University.
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher who was educated at the Lycée du Parc and the École Normale Supérieure.

Jean-Louis Burnouf studied under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He served as professor of rhetoric at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, held the chair of Latin eloquence at Collège de France (1816–1844), and was university librarian at the Sorbonne.
Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held a post at the CNRS.
Jean-Luc Chevillard is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Culioli. He worked as a researcher at the CNRS from circa 1990 to 2021.

Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology who studied under Bernard Frank. He worked at the CNRS, served as a director of studies at EPHE, and held a professorship at the Collège de France (2010–2022).

Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a Sinologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the Chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as conservator and president at the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under Yves Hervouet and at INALCO. He served as president of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 1998 to 2004.

Jeannine Auboyer was an Indologist and art historian educated at EPHE and the École du Louvre under Joseph Hackin, Paul Pelliot, and others. She was chief curator at Musée Guimet (1965–1980) and held a chair at École du Louvre.
